runs.text: In year 37, early winter, morning, at Harum, the winter camp of the Kesh band, Imra was shaping a scraper by striking cutting stone against a lump of heavy yellow stone. Sparks fell on dry moss beside her, and the moss began to smoke. Imra blew on the smoking moss, and it caught fire. She tried again three times that day, and the moss caught fire two of those times. Tavu saw it. Before this, the Kesh band kept fire only by carrying embers from camp to camp. This was the first time anyone in the world made fire by striking stones. Imra believed fire lives inside the heavy yellow stone, but was not sure.

Year 37. Early winter morning. Harum. Winter camp of the Kesh band. Imra was shaping a scraper. She struck cutting stone against a lump of heavy yellow stone. Sparks fell on dry moss. Moss began to smoke. Imra blew on the smoking moss. It caught fire. She tried again three times that day. Moss caught fire two of those times. Tavu saw it. Before this, the Kesh band kept fire by carrying embers. This was the first time anyone in the world made fire by striking stones. Imra believed fire lives inside the heavy yellow stone.

In year 41, during deep winter night, death from cold occurred at Harum, the old winter camp of the Kesh band. Oru, a man of the Kesh band, had broken his leg in a fall in autumn, and subsequently could not walk far. Food ran out at Harum, so the Kesh band moved to Ulmeke, a walk of 4 days. The band left Oru behind at Harum with a small fire and 2 strips of dried meat. Sefi was the last to leave him. On his 4th night alone, the fire went out and Oru died of cold. Ten days later, 2 hunters of the band found his body beside the dead fire.

We tell the story. Year 41. Deep winter, night. Harum. Cold hollow. Old winter camp of the Kesh band. Oru, man, 58 years old. Oru broke his leg in a fall in autumn. After that, he could not walk far. Food ran out at Harum. Kesh band moved to Ulmeke. Walk of 4 days. Band left Oru behind at Harum. Small fire. 2 strips of dried meat. Sefi was the last to leave him. On his 4th night alone, the fire went out. Oru died of cold. 10 days later, 2 hunters of the band found his body beside the dead fire.

In year 52, spring, night, at Sefa, a lake, the Tulo band camped on its shore. Kaya, a woman of the Tulo band, gave birth to a girl in the camp on the shore of Sefa. Anwe, a woman of the Tulo band, and Lisu, a woman of the Tulo band, helped her. The labour lasted most of the night. The girl was small, and she cried at once. She is the 2nd child of Kaya. The first, a boy, is 3 years old. The Tulo band believed a child is given a name only after it lives through its first winter.

We tell the story. Year 52. Spring. Night. We were at Sefa. Sefa is wide water. We camped on its shore. Kaya gave birth. A girl came. Anwe and Lisu helped her. The labour lasted most of the night. The girl was small. She cried at once. She is the 2nd child of Kaya. The first child is a boy. The girl has no name yet. We believe a child is given a name only after it lives through its first winter.

In year 63, late summer, dusk, an event occurred at Teshu, a ford of the river. Anuk, a man of the Kesh band, waited for Moro, a man of the Tulo band. When Moro came to cross, Anuk killed him with a spear thrust to the belly. The spear had a cutting stone point. Moro died at the ford before dark. Ishe, a woman of the Tulo band, saw the killing from the far bank. Ishe ran to the Tulo camp and told them. Anuk believed and was sure that Moro killed his brother Pell in the spring.

We tell the story. Year 63. Late summer. Dusk. At Teshu, a ford of the river. Anuk waited for Moro. Moro came to cross. Anuk killed Moro. Anuk used a spear. The spear had a cutting stone point. Anuk killed Moro with the spear thrust to the belly. Moro died at the ford before dark. Ishe saw the killing from the far bank. Ishe ran to the Tulo camp. Ishe told them.

In year 70, autumn, the Amaru band, consisting of 26 people, argued for 2 days at Ulmeke, a cliff with dry caves, regarding where to spend the winter. Hesh, a man of 40 years old, of the Amaru band, wanted to go to Kotara, the sea shore, which was a 6 days' walk away. Nima, a woman of 46 years old, of the Amaru band, wanted to stay at Ulmeke. The band split: 11 people went with Hesh to Kotara, and 15 stayed with Nima at Ulmeke. Rafi, the son of Hesh, stayed with Nima. Hesh believed and was sure that the shellfish at Kotara do not run out in winter. Nima believed and was sure that the walk to Kotara is too long for the old and for small children.

We were at Ulmeke. Year 70, autumn. The Amaru band, twenty-six people. We argued two days. Where to spend winter. Hesh wanted Kotara. Nima wanted Ulmeke. Hesh said, "The shellfish at Kotara do not run out in winter." Nima said, "The walk to Kotara is too long for the old and for small children." We split. Eleven people went with Hesh to Kotara. Fifteen stayed with Nima at Ulmeke. Rafi, Hesh's son, stayed with Nima. This is how it was.

In year 77, late winter, a night occurred at Sefa, a lake frozen over. Dabo, a man of the Kesh band, planned to cross the frozen lake Sefa to hunt on the far shore, as crossing the ice saves a day of walking. The night before, Dabo dreamt that his dead mother Ama stood on the ice, and the ice broke under her. Upon waking, Dabo changed his mind and did not cross the ice. Instead, he walked around the lake, which took him 2 days. That same morning, Pek and Hanu crossed the ice and came back safely. Before the dream, Dabo believed the ice is strong enough to cross. After the dream, Dabo believed but was not sure that the ice will break.

We tell of a dream. Year 77. Late winter, night. Sefa, wide water, frozen lake. Dabo planned to cross the ice. He would hunt on the far shore. Crossing the ice saves a day of walking. The night before, Dabo dreamt. His dead mother Ama stood on the ice. The ice broke under her. When he woke, Dabo changed his mind. He did not cross the ice. He walked around the lake instead. That took him 2 days. Pek and Hanu crossed the ice. They came back safely.

In year 118, winter, night, at Harum, the winter camp of the Kesh band, Shana told the story to 14 listeners. Shana told Tara-mi, first told in year 45, by Imra. The old telling stated, "Fire lived inside the heavy yellow stone." Imra struck the stone, and fire jumped into the moss. The telling now stated, "The sky put fire inside the heavy yellow stone." The first mother struck the stone, and fire jumped into the dry grass. This change meant the sky was added as the one who put fire in the stone; the name Imra was lost, and she became the first mother; the moss became dry grass.

We tell the story. Year 118. Winter night. Harum. Winter camp of the Kesh band. Shana told Tara-mi to fourteen listeners. Tara-mi. First told in year 45. Imra told it. Old telling: Fire lived inside the heavy yellow stone. A woman named Imra struck the stone. Fire jumped into the moss. Now: The sky put fire inside the heavy yellow stone. The first mother struck the stone. Fire jumped into the dry grass. The sky was added. Imra name lost. She became the first mother. Moss became dry grass.

In year 90, summer, afternoon, at Ulmeke, the camp of the Amaru band, a storm occurred. A sky-fire struck a lone tall tree on the ridge above the camp. The tree split and burned. No one was hurt. Nima, a woman of the Amaru band, said the sky-fire was a sign that the dead no longer wanted the band at Ulmeke. Seventeen of the twenty people of the Amaru band came to believe her. Three days later, the band left Ulmeke and walked toward Sefa. Nima believed the sky-fire was a sign that the dead no longer want the band at Ulmeke, and seventeen of the twenty people of the Amaru band believed the same as Nima.

Year 90. Summer. Afternoon. At Ulmeke. The camp of the Amaru band. A storm. Sky-fire struck a lone tall tree on the ridge above the camp. The tree split. The tree burned. No one was hurt. Nima said the sky-fire was a sign. The dead no longer wanted the band at Ulmeke. Seventeen of the twenty people of the Amaru band came to believe her. Three days later, the band left Ulmeke. We walked toward Sefa.

In year 95, late autumn, before dawn, seven men of the Kesh band, led by Kelo, attacked the Tulo camp at Sefa, a lake. Kelo killed Gudo with clubs. Rena and Oshi were taken captive and their hands were tied with sinew cord. Rena and Oshi carried the dried meat of the Tulo band to the Kesh camp. The other Tulo people fled into the reeds. Kelo believed the Tulo camp had more dried meat than it needed.

We tell the story. Year 95. Late autumn. Before dawn. Kesh band. Seven men. Kelo led. Kelo attacked Tulo camp at Sefa. They killed Gudo with clubs. They took Rena and Oshi captive. They tied their hands with sinew cord. Rena and Oshi carry dried meat of Tulo band to Kesh camp. Other Tulo people fled into the reeds. Kelo knew Tulo camp had more dried meat than it needed.

In year 102, spring, midday, a meeting occurred at Teshu, a ford of the river. The Kesh band and the Amaru band met by chance. The two groups had no words in common, so they pointed and laid things on the ground. Temo, a man of the Kesh band, gave Yari, a woman of the Amaru band, 3 lumps of red earth. Yari gave Temo a string of 12 white shells from Kotara, the sea shore. The two bands camped apart for 1 night and went their separate ways the next morning.

We met at Teshu. Spring. Midday. Kesh band and Amaru band met. No words in common. We pointed. We laid things on the ground. Temo gave Yari three lumps of red earth. Yari gave Temo a string of twelve white shells from Kotara. We camped apart for one night. We went our separate ways the next morning.
